units.title: Prejudice and Discrimination
units.intro: Grammar: subject–verb agreement in complex sentences, and the present perfect and past perfect passive.

cards.title: Agreement in complex sentences
rule: Find the **real subject** even when other words come between it and the verb: *The **rights** of every citizen **are** protected.* *The **list** of complaints **is** long.*
A relative clause verb agrees with its antecedent: *people who **are** ...; a person who **is** ...*. A title or name of one thing is singular: *“Things Fall Apart” **is** a famous novel.*

examples.text: The attitude of some people is unfair.
One of the girls is absent.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Aster ________ in this biotechnology laboratory since she graduated from university five years ago.

steps.text: The time-marker 'since she graduated' indicates an action that started in the past and continues to the present, requiring the Present Perfect Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{has/have been} + \text{V-ing}$$).
Students often see 'is working' (Option A) and choose it because they think of it as an ongoing present action.
However, 'since' requires the perfect aspect, making 'has been working' (Option C) correct.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The construction company ________ the new highway road project three weeks ago.

steps.text: The definite past time-marker 'three weeks ago' requires the Simple Past tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_2$$).
Students often confuse Present Perfect 'has completed' (Option A) with Simple Past 'completed' (Option B).
Present Perfect cannot be used with definite past time-markers like 'three weeks ago'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Look at those thick dark clouds hanging over the mountains! It ________ rain very soon.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a future prediction based on clear, present physical evidence ('thick dark clouds'). This requires 'be going to' ($$\text{S} + \text{be going to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'will' (Option A) for all future predictions. However, when there is clear physical evidence in the present, 'be going to' (Option B) is the grammatically correct choice.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ኣብቲ ከባቢ ንጹር ዝኾነ ናይ ዓይኒ መርትዖ (thick dark clouds - ጸሊም ደበና) ስለ ዘሎ፡ ንመጻኢ ትንቢት ክንገልጽ ከለና 'be going to' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። መርትዖ ምስ ዘይህሉ ግን 'will' ምጥቃም ቅኑዕ ምኾነ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The public train to Djibouti ________ from the main station at exactly 7:30 AM tomorrow.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The departure of a public train is a formal, timetabled future event that is outside of personal control. This requires the Present Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'tomorrow' and automatically choose 'will depart' (Option C) or 'is departing' (Option A). However, formal timetables and schedules must be expressed in the Present Simple.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ናይ ባቡር ወይ ነፋሪት መገሻ (timetable) ቀዋሚ ስርዓት ዘለዎ ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ንመጻኢ ግዜ ክንገልጽ ከለና ብ Present Simple 'departs' (Option B) ጥራይ ኢና ክንጽሕፍ ዘለና። 'tomorrow' ስለ ዘሎ 'will depart' ምምራጽ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The houses that my uncle built ____ very strong.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The main subject is "The houses" (plural).

**Step 2:** "that my uncle built" is a relative clause and does not change agreement.

**Step 3:** So the verb is "are".

**Tip:** In long sentences, find the head noun of the subject and make the verb agree with it. Perfect passives: has/have/had + been + past participle.

lessons.title: Present perfect and past perfect passive

cards.title: Present perfect and past perfect passive
rule: **has/have been + pp:** *New laws **have been passed** to stop discrimination.* **had been + pp:** *Before 1991 many people **had been denied** their rights.*

examples.text: Women have been given equal rights.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "The rule had been change."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** **has/have been + pp:** *New laws **have been passed** to stop discrimination.* **had been + pp:** *Before 1991 many people **had been denied** their rights.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "The rule had been change." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "The rule had been changed."

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **Cross out** the words between the subject and verb, then check agreement.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Find the real subject before choosing the verb: one of, the number of and titles are singular; a number of is plural. Present perfect passive = has/have been + pp; past perfect passive = had been + pp.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The number of students _______ greater this year than that of last year.
cards.why:
There is a specific rule for 'The number of' vs 'A number of':
1. **'The number of'** takes a **singular verb** (referring to the specific total).
2. **'A number of'** takes a **plural verb** (meaning 'many').
Since it refers to 'this year', the singular present verb **'is'** is correct.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: We have invited all of the students in this school for the New Year celebration.

options.A: All of the students in this school has been invited for the New Year celebration.
options.B: All of the students in this school had been invited for the New Year celebration.
options.C: All of the students in this school have been invited for the New Year celebration.
options.D: This school has been invited for the New Year celebration.
options.E: This school has invited all the students for the New Year celebration.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Tense is **Present Perfect** ("have invited").
**Step 2:** The passive structure is **have/has been + V3**.
**Step 3:** The new subject is "All of the students" (plural), so we use "have been invited". Choice A is wrong because it uses 'has' for a plural subject.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A large number of deaths have been caused by road accidents.

options.A: Road accidents are causing a large number of deaths.
options.B: Road accidents cause a large number of deaths.
options.C: Road accidents have caused a large number of deaths.
options.D: Road accidents had caused a large number of deaths.
options.E: Road accidents are causes of a large number of deaths.

cards.why: The sentence is in the Present Perfect Passive ('have been caused'). To change it to Active Voice, keep the Present Perfect tense: 'Subject + have/has + past participle'.

questions.q: Read: "Prejudice is an opinion formed without knowledge or reason. A person who judges others by their skin colour, religion or language, before getting to know them, shows prejudice. Education and contact between groups can reduce it." According to the passage, what can reduce prejudice?
questions.label: 16. Read: "Prejudice is an opinion formed without knowledge or reason. A person who judges others by…

similar.q: Define prejudice using the passage.
similar.a: An opinion formed without knowledge or reason.

similar.q: Find a relative clause in the passage.
similar.a: who judges others by their skin colour, religion or language.

why: Answer B: education and contact between groups
The last sentence says "Education and contact between groups can reduce it".
The other options describe prejudice itself.
So the first option is correct.
